reference_opening.argument: The video promotes and demonstrates a cryptocurrency bot presented as able to bypass token taxes and other anti-bot controls while automating conditional purchases and subsequent token sales. The demonstrated participation flow involves configuring a contract and tax threshold, monitoring stated conditions, sending a purchase transaction, and using a hotkey to sell the token position. The speaker directs interested viewers to contact or join the associated community, although the supplied records do not establish payment terms, actual profitability, victim losses, or the outcome of any blockchain transaction.

citations.quote: today I will show you the ChainSniperBot version 0.9.5
I will deploy this contract now. Okay. So now I have this contract address.
I enter my contract address here. And then the bot will start to scan this contract.
I want to buy only if the tax is under 20%
The tax for buying and the tax for selling is under 20%. Then the bot will. Send the transaction.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present this as a guaranteed-profit trade. He explicitly reports a negative result in the demonstration, rather than concealing it, and distinguishes the displayed profit from a figure that includes sell tax. He also qualifies the bot’s reach by acknowledging an exception. Those admissions matter: the video shows a tool with conditions and limitations, not a promise that viewers will make money by using it.

So the real profit is when you include the sell tax.
usually we can snipe almost every token like this every antibody token. With this mod uh there is just one exception but i will talk later

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited contract address, tax threshold, and transaction describe a conditional test of software. They do not establish that the speaker promises a return or asks viewers to put funds into his custody. The opening also omits the reported negative profit—the opposite of a demonstrated winning trade.

citations.quote: So we have a profit negative because it's a new token.
I want to buy only if the tax is under 20%

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A negative displayed profit and a briefly mentioned exception do not turn this into a risk warning. The speaker still presents a bot that monitors buy and sell tax, then sends a purchase transaction when his threshold is met; he also demonstrates selling the token position. The defense’s quotes limit what can be claimed about guaranteed returns, but they do not erase the promoted trading-bot workflow.

citations.quote: The tax for buying and the tax for selling is under 20%. Then the bot will. Send the transaction.
And then if I press Ctrl Q, the transaction is sent already and sold.

opening.argument: Judge, the center of this video is an operational walkthrough. The speaker says he is answering questions about Easy Mode and will demonstrate it, then deploys his own contract, enters its address, and explains what the bot scans. He manually changes the contract’s tax to show why the bot waits before buying. That staged sequence is evidence of teaching how a conditional trading tool behaves; it is not, by itself, an instruction for viewers to buy a particular token.

citations.quote: I had a lot of questions about the easy mode,. How it works. I will make a demonstration just now.
I will deploy this contract now. Okay. So now I have this contract address.
And then the bot will start to scan this contract.
So I will do it manually now. I will remove the tax. So I will just put 1%.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening accurately describes a purchase threshold and a sell hotkey, but those steps are also what a functional tutorial would need to explain. The speaker describes creating the pool himself and manually changing its tax. That controlled setup gives the transaction sequence a narrower meaning than proof of a viewer-facing investment offer.

citations.quote: I supply my liquidity, I create a pool.
So I will do it manually now. I will remove the tax.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A staged demonstration can still promote a trading bot. The speaker presents the controlled example as showing how the bot responds to tax changes, buys a token, and makes it available to sell. He also characterizes the feature as a way to bypass anti-bot measures. No particular token recommendation is necessary for the video to promote that trading workflow.

citations.quote: with this mode, you have to know it can bypass all the anti-bot measures,. Like the tax, like the delay at trading and many others.

opening.argument: Judge, the invitation at the end is to ask questions and contact a bot-user community, not to send the speaker a deposit. The description supplies contact details, while the walkthrough describes a wallet and transactions involved in using the tool. Nothing in the supplied material specifies a purchase price, a guaranteed return, a request for credentials, or a recruitment payout. On this record, the contact invitation is consistent with support for a software product; it does not establish an investment scheme.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening identifies a bot-assisted trade, but its transaction quote does not show money being entrusted to the speaker. Its contract and threshold quotes show configuration, not a promised payout. The speaker’s closing invitation is to contact the community with questions; the supplied record does not turn that invitation into evidence of a deposit or guaranteed-return offer.

citations.quote: Then the bot will. Send the transaction.
So you can join us, you can ask us questions.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a shown deposit, credential request, or guaranteed payout limits the conclusion, but it does not make the content merely customer support. The speaker showcases a bot that conditionally purchases tokens, tracks profit, and offers a sell command, then invites viewers to contact the associated community. Those are the video’s affirmative trading-bot promotion and workflow, regardless of whether its commercial terms are disclosed.
